To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proliferative capacity, measured as the S-phase fraction (SF), of breast carcinomas is closely correlated with NG, as determined by the Bloom-Richardson method, with the highest SF found in high-grade (Grade 3) tumors.
nuclear grade is a reliable indicator of the proliferative capacity and the presence of p53 in invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast.

the presence of p53 in breast carcinoma is associated with elevated SPF and is associated with overexpression of the EGFR, but not with overexpression of c-erb-B2, and that p53 is present in only 13% of breast carcinomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms that control cell growth, differentiation, and death.
the development of a new method of measuring the proliferation of cancer cells.
the study of the expression of oncogenes and tumor-suppressor genes in breast carcinomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NG and SPF are the best indicators of the proliferative potential of breast cancer, and that EGFR and c-erb B-2 are associated with the presence of p53.
the presence of p53, EGFR, or c-erb-B2 is associated with high NG and elevated SPF, and that p53, EGFr, and c- erbB-2 may be useful in the prognostic assessment of breast carcinoma.
the presence of p53, EGFR, and c- erbB-2 in breast cancer is associated with an increased proliferative rate, which is a poor prognostic sign.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an association between high NG and high SPF, and that p53, EGFR, and c- erb-B-2 are all associated with high SPF.
there is a correlation between nuclear grade, proliferating cell index and p53.
the expression of p53 and the EGFR is correlated to the proliferative activity of the tumor, as determined by SPF, and is associated with high-grade tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlation between nuclear grade and S-phase is very high, and that this relationship is more robust than the correlation between S-phase and proliferating cell nuclear protein.
the expression of EGFR and p53 in breast carcinoma is correlated with a high grade of nuclear atypia, a high proliferative index and the presence of aneuploidy.
we can now predict which patients will benefit most from chemotherapy and which patients will not.
